title: fix(platform-objects): stale hand-authored translations fall back to the source string (#8765)
body:
Fixes #8765

Implements the ruled **Option B** (delegated adjudication, comment `5299847077`): *record the source hash at translation time; a hash mismatch marks the translation stale, and stale falls back to the source text.*

## The hole

The `apps` / `dashboards` / `pages` half of this package's i18n is hand-authored per locale, and every gate over it judges **presence or ownership** — `app-nav-translation-parity.test.ts`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:app-nav-i18n`. A translated value that has gone **stale** satisfies all of them: it is present, it is owned, it is not untranslated. So a source-string edit left `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` serving the previous translation indefinitely under a green build.

## Where the resolution seam turned out to be

The dispatch asked for this to be established first, because it decides the shape. Traced: nothing in `packages/platform-objects` resolves a locale. `TranslationBundle` is consumed by `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`, whose lookups walk a chain (requested locale → `fallbackChain`, default `['en']` → the metadata literal) and return the first non-empty candidate. `plugin.ts` hands `SetupAppTranslations` to the kernel i18n service at `kernel:ready`, one locale at a time.

That mattered, because the obvious shape — a hash key on each translated leaf — is **not available**. `TranslationData`'s leaves are `strictObject` shapes closed to their declared keys (`navigation` leaves accept `label` and nothing else), so a per-leaf hash would require editing `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` **and** the resolver, both outside this card's surface, and would have taken the extractor with it.

So the hash lives in a **sidecar module** instead, and staleness resolves at bundle assembly — `setup.translation.ts`, the package's own serving seam. The emitted bundle stays an ordinary `TranslationData`. **No spec change, no resolver change, no extractor change: the `scripts/**` fork the dispatch flagged did not fire, and `check:i18n` is green.**

## The mechanism

- Each translated locale ships a `*.source-hashes.ts` table recording, per leaf, the digest of the `en.ts` source string that leaf was translated from. `en` is a copy of the source rather than a translation of it, and two assertions already hold it there (this file's own default-locale block for `apps.*` / `dashboards.*`; `check:app-nav-i18n` for `pages.*`), so hashing `en` transitively hashes the declared source with no cross-package import.
- `withSourceFallback` substitutes the **source string** for any leaf whose recorded digest disagrees with the current source.
- **A missing hash is legacy-trusted, not stale.** Backfilled once from the then-current source: 125 leaves per locale, so nothing degraded on landing.
- **Recovery is per-locale.** The tables are per-locale, so updating one translation's value *and* its hash restores that locale alone.

### Why it substitutes rather than deletes the key

Both spellings serve identical text — a deleted leaf falls through the resolver chain, and every link in that chain is the source string. Substitution is chosen because it moves **no key set**: every gate over these bundles, plus `packages/cli/test/platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts`, makes key-set claims, and deletion would move them as a side effect of a value-level rule — turning translation lag into a red build, the Option C cost the ruling rejected.

### The acceptance criterion

B introduces no visibly third state. A translated locale carrying the source string verbatim is exactly what the extractor already writes for an untranslated key under `--fill=default`, and exactly what the locale chain has always rendered. The one live-data behavioural assertion is that the served bundle carries exactly the authored key set — a content edit cannot trip it, only a bug in the mechanism can.

Every behavioural claim runs on **synthetic** bundles, deliberately: an assertion that nothing is currently stale would go red on any un-re-translated source edit, which is Option C wearing a different hat. `source-hash.test.ts` says so, and names the two consistency checks it declines to make and why.

## Reverse verification, direction predicted before running

Prediction: a realistic source edit leaves the suite **green** while changing what is served — the non-red direction is the whole point of B over C.

Edited `API Keys` to `API Credentials` at the source (`account.app.ts`) **and** in the pinned `en.ts` copy, touching no translation and no hash table:

| | before edit | after edit |
|---|---|---|
| `en.ts` source | `API Keys` | `API Credentials` |
| `zh-CN.ts` authored | `API 密钥` | `API 密钥` (untouched) |
| **served `zh-CN`** | `API 密钥` | **`API Credentials`** |
| stale leaves | 0 | 1 (that path) |
| full suite | 22 files / 394 tests green | **24 / 410 green** |

Both directions confirmed: the mechanism is inert while the backfill holds, fires on exactly the edited leaf, and fails no build. Restored from the commit afterwards (`git checkout` from the branch, never the shared stash); working tree verified clean.

`check:i18n` first refused to measure (`@objectstack/cli` not built) and said so explicitly — including that piping it reports the pipe's status. Built the CLI and re-ran with the real exit code; the EXIT values above are the gates', not a pipe's.

The re-measure notes a pre-existing lowerable `@objectstack/lint` TEST_DEBT entry (records 20, measures 19) and 1 raw error below its ceiling. Both pre-date this PR, are outside its file surface, and lowering a ledger is not this seat's call — left untouched.

**Gate families re-derived** against the real changed paths with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`. It surfaced five the dispatch prompt could not have named, because no changeset existed when the prompt's derivation ran — all green:

```
pnpm check:changeset-gate-self-tests        EXIT=0
pnpm check:objectui-changeset               EXIT=0
node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs EXIT=0  (no declared-breaking changeset)
node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs    EXIT=0
node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs       EXIT=0
```

## Notes

- **#8861 landed mid-flight and its new sentence is updated here, as instructed.** At dispatch it was open and unmerged (base `51bb277ef`, same as mine); it merged into `main` while this was in progress and came in with my `origin/main` merge, cleanly. Its clause *"per-locale coverage of those `pages.*` keys ... remains unasserted anywhere in this repo"* is now qualified rather than deleted: the **coverage** half stays true, but those six leaves per locale do carry recorded hashes, so their **freshness** is no longer unjudged. Verified the six `pages.*` entries exist in each table before writing the claim.
- Also updated the older clause in the same file stating the question was undecided — it named #8765 as the open decision.
- `*.generated.ts` untouched; the generated half cannot have this hole (`en` is rewritten every extract, #8543).
- A changeset is included: this is user-visible behaviour.
